result:
Solution 1 is wrong. It claims P(c) fails for every c, which would make α infinite. But the cycle C_n has treewidth 2 and admits a width-2 tree decomposition (a path of triangles) in which every vertex has spread at most 3. So the cycle is not a counterexample, and the claimed Ω(log n) spread lower bound is false.

Solution 2 claims α = 1 and that P(c) holds for every c > 1. This contradicts what I recall of the known result. P(c) is known to be achievable at width about 2·tw(G)+1, but impossible for c below 2, which means the true threshold is 2. This is from memory and I have not re-derived it. Its "P(c) holds for c > 1" argument is only a sketch for grids and does not handle general graphs.

Solution 3 claims α = 3 and cites IMC 2011 Problem 10, which has nothing to do with this question. The value 3 is unsupported.

By my recollection the correct value is α = 2, which none of the three solutions gives.

CHOICE: NONE
